title: Subdivisions Further Subdivided by Place
summary: Subdivisions marked (May Subd Geog) on free-floating lists or in the subject authority file may themselves be followed by a place: [topic]--[subdivision]--[place]. With multiple topical subdivisions, the geographic subdivision follows the last subdivision authorized for subdivision by place; otherwise it is interposed after the main heading (H 870). The standard order is [topic]--[place]--[chronology]--[form]. The 1977-1989 practice of placing the place both before and after a subdivision is discontinued.
validation_rules: The standard order of elements is `[topic]--[place]--[chronology]--[form]` (adopted 1992). (H 860 Background)

A topical subdivision may be followed by a geographic subdivision only if it is authorized for further subdivision by place: free-floating subdivisions marked `(May Subd Geog)` on the lists in H 1095-H 1200, or subdivisions so authorized in the subject authority file: e.g. `Construction industry--Law and legislation--Maryland`; `Chemistry--Study and teaching--Maryland`. (H 860 Background, sec. 1, 2)

When a heading has more than one topical subdivision and a place, place the geographic subdivision after the last subdivision authorized for further subdivision by place; if none is so authorized, interpose the place after the main heading (H 870). (H 860 sec. 3)

Examples from the educational-institutions pattern (H 1151.5), where `--Finance` is not divisible by place but `--Finance--Law and legislation (May Subd Geog)`, `--Services for (May Subd Geog)`, `--Services for--Contracting out (May Subd Geog)` are: `Medical colleges--California--Finance`; `Medical colleges--Finance--Law and legislation--California`; `Universities and colleges--Services for--Minnesota`; `Universities and colleges--Services for--Contracting out--Minnesota`. (H 860 sec. 3)

Do not place a geographic subdivision both before and after the same subdivision (e.g. `Black people--Latin America--Study and teaching--United States`); this 1977-1989 practice was discontinued in 1989. (H 860 Background Note)
[LC practice] Correct bibliographic records that do not conform to current instructions for further geographic subdivision. (H 860 sec. 3 [LC practice])

sections.heading: 1. Free-floating subdivisions
sections.text:
Free-floating subdivisions that are authorized for further geographic subdivision have the notation (May Subd Geog) on the lists of free-floating subdivisions in H 1095-H 1200. Use these subdivisions divided by place if required by the work in hand. Example:

```
650 #0 $a Chemistry $x Study and teaching $z Maryland.
```

sections.heading: 2. Non-free-floating subdivisions
sections.text: Use subdivisions that are established in the subject authority file with authorization for geographic subdivision divided by place when needed. When establishing new main heading-non-free-floating subdivision combinations, follow the instructions in H 364 sec. 1 to authorize further subdivision by place when appropriate.

sections.heading: 3. Multiple topical subdivisions
sections.text:
When combining a main heading with a place name and more than one topical subdivision, place any needed geographic subdivisions following the last subdivision that is authorized for further subdivision by place. For example, the following subdivisions are on the pattern heading list of free-floating subdivisions used under types of educational institutions (H 1151.5):

```
--Finance
--Finance--Law and legislation (May Subd Geog)
--Services for (May Subd Geog)
--Services for--Contracting out (May Subd Geog)
```

Therefore, the following headings may be constructed:

```
650 #0 $a Medical colleges $z California $x Finance.
650 #0 $a Medical colleges $x Finance $x Law and legislation $z California.
650 #0 $a Universities and colleges $x Services for $z Minnesota.
650 #0 $a Universities and colleges $x Services for $x Contracting out $z Minnesota.
```

sections.heading: 3. Bibliographic file maintenance
sections.text: LC practice: Correct any bibliographic records encountered in the database that do not conform to current instructions for further geographic subdivision.
